frequency_question: How often do regulatory principals with zero-setting discretion activate or raise the countercyclical capital buffer above zero during periods of sustained economic expansion within their respective jurisdictions?
membership_rule: Includes independent central banks and regulatory authorities with explicit statutory power to set a CCyB rate between 0% and higher, operating under standard Basel III frameworks. Excludes jurisdictions where the buffer rate is tied automatically to mechanical indicators without principal discretion or where authorities lack the statutory power.

cases.name: Reserve Bank of New Zealand CCyB activation
Swiss National Bank / FINMA CCyB activation

provenance_note: claims 60 cases from only 5 named (12.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 14 named or estimated across major jurisdictions; covers G20 and advanced OECD banking systems.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller emerging markets with nascent macroprudential frameworks.
skeleton: Major advanced economy regulatory jurisdictions with independent macroprudential mandate (approx. 30 jurisdictions) observed across two distinct economic expansion phases post-Basel III implementation.
multiplier: 30 jurisdictions times 2 expansion phases = 60 opportunities; fewer than 15 instances of active upward adjustment from zero during non-crisis expansions.
validity_reason: Macroprudential institutional frameworks and central bank governance structures evolve slowly over multi-year horizons.
